claims.statement: The guide applies to FPT, GHES and GHEC. Cloud-only author-options content allows choosing a verified author email for UI file operations or pull-request merge when privacy is disabled; with privacy enabled author email cannot be changed and defaults to noreply.

The web settings sequence uses Settings, Emails, add-and-verify and primary selection; cloud-only privacy selection remains distinct. Source screenshots illustrate navigation, not actual configured or verified target state.
Git email changes affect future command-line commits; previous commits retain the earlier email. A current setting cannot certify historical scrubbing.

The global Git configuration example sets user.email for repositories on the computer and reads it back; the single-repository example first enters the repository, sets local user.email and reads it back. Local settings override global for that repository without affecting other repositories.
The terminal reusable distinguishes Terminal on macOS/Linux and Git Bash on Windows. Command snippets are source data and are not executed during ingestion or authorized configuration changes.
The set-email reusable allows any email and adds the noreply alternative only for cloud products; attribution requires adding the address to the GitHub account through the separate procedure.

Read-back of a Git setting is configuration evidence, not proof of correct account authorization, mailbox verification, future push safety or signature verification. Linked reference and Git-username guidance need separate review.
